mechanism_narrative: Lower FEDFUNDS levels correlate with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to compressed discount rates and accommodative monetary policy.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS level is not inversely related to 20-day returns: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or t-test of returns in low-rate periods vs. baseline shows no significant difference (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL exceeding 225 signals elevated inflation that triggers monetary tightening expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 225 does not predict negative returns: 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent low unemployment (UNRATE < 5.0%) and strong employment growth (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly) indicates a tight labor market driving positive equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction of UNRATE < 5.0% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% does not predict positive returns: 60-day returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 0.5% and rising for 3 consecutive months) trigger reduced liquidity and higher risk aversion, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 0.5 AND FEDFUNDS has risen for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 0.5% and rising for 3 months) does not predict negative returns: 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.03.
